abertura: In the lesson you are going to talk for two minutes about yourself and what you want to do, to someone your age who has never been to Brazil.
Three of the sentences below are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: You have to know what you want to do before you can talk about it.
itens.porque: Not being sure is one of the things you talk about. In the lesson you will find a sentence for exactly that, and it is one of the most useful ones there is.

itens.t: Saying why you want something makes the answer more interesting than saying what.
itens.porque: I want to study medicine ends there. Because what I like is helping someone gives the other person something to ask about.

itens.t: If someone asks you something you had not thought about, it is better to change the subject.
itens.porque: Changing the subject is what ends a conversation. There are three or four short phrases that buy you time instead, and you already used them last lesson.

itens.t: The person listening will ask about the part you said least about.
itens.porque: That is how conversations work, and it is why the short answer is the risky one: it is exactly what gets picked.

itens.t: Two minutes is a long time to talk about yourself.
itens.porque: It is. It is roughly six or seven sentences said slowly, and until now you have been stopping at two or three.

itens.t: You should have the whole thing memorized before you speak.
itens.porque: Memorized answers fall apart at the first unexpected question — and there is one in this lesson, on purpose.

sec1.pt: Na aula você vai falar dois minutos sobre você e sobre o que quer fazer, para alguém da sua idade que nunca veio ao Brasil. Antes disso, marque as três frases verdadeiras.

nota.titulo: Por que esta é a aula que fecha o bloco
nota.texto: As três anteriores foram sobre falar de um filme, sustentar uma conversa e fazer perguntas. Esta é sobre você — e é aqui que se vê o que ficou das outras três.

sec2.titulo: Six words for what comes after school

itens.t: to apply
alts: to ask officially to join something
to be accepted by a university
itens.ok: to ask officially to join something

itens.t: a degree
alts: what you get at the end of university
the number of years a course lasts
itens.ok: what you get at the end of university

itens.t: an internship
alts: the first job you are paid for
a short period working to learn a job
itens.ok: a short period working to learn a job

itens.t: a gap year
alts: a year between school and university
a year you have to repeat
itens.ok: a year between school and university

itens.t: to make up your mind
alts: to change your plan
to finally decide

itens.t: to work out
alts: to be hard work
to end well

sec2.pt: Seis palavras sobre o que vem depois da escola. Escolha o sentido que cabe. A última, to work out, aparece na pergunta mais difícil da aula.

nota.texto: Uma delas é academia. A outra é a desta aula: if it does not work out — se não der certo. É a pergunta que a Nina faz e que quase ninguém consegue responder de improviso, nem em português.

abertura: Complete the six sentences with the words from activity two.
Write them about you, if they are true. If they are not, leave them as they are.

itens.t: I have to {apply|90px} for a place before the end of the year.
A {degree|90px} in that takes five years here.
I might do an {internship|110px} first, to see what the job is really like.
Some people take a {gap|70px} year before they start.
I still have not made up my {mind|80px}.
If it does not {work|80px} out, I would do something else with people in it.

sec3.pt: Complete as seis frases com as palavras do exercício 2. Escreva sobre você, se forem verdadeiras. Se não forem, deixe como estão.

nota.titulo: A quinta e a sexta são as difíceis
nota.texto: As quatro primeiras são informação. As duas últimas são dúvida — e dizer que você ainda não decidiu, em inglês, sem parar a frase, é metade do que esta aula faz.

abertura: Six questions someone might ask you at a break. Which ones are about your life now, and which ones are about what comes after school?

itens.t: What subjects do you do?
itens.porque: Present, and about this year. It is the easy one, and it is almost always the first question.

itens.t: Are you going to apply this year?
itens.porque: Going to for a plan that is already fairly decided. Notice the order: the auxiliary is in front of the subject, exactly as in the last lesson.

itens.t: How many people are in your class?
itens.porque: A fact about today, and the shortest answer on this list. Say only the number and the conversation stops.

itens.t: Have you made up your mind yet?
itens.porque: Yet is what makes it about later: it assumes a decision that has not happened. It is also the politest way of asking.

itens.t: Do you like your school?
itens.porque: An opinion question about now. This is where a reason belongs, and the whole first lesson of this block was about that.

itens.t: What would you do if it does not work out?
itens.porque: The hardest one on the list, and the one Nina asks in the lesson. It is about a future that has not happened and might not.

sec4.rationale: The three about now can be answered with a fact. The three about later cannot — all of them need a reason or a doubt, and that is what makes them harder.
sec4.pt: Seis perguntas que alguém pode fazer no intervalo. Diga quais são sobre a sua vida agora e quais são sobre o que vem depois da escola.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. These five are the shapes you can use in your lesson.

itens.t: I am in
alts: the last year of school my
my last year of school
my last school year of

itens.t: I want to study biology,
alts: because of I like the lab part
for I like the lab part
because I like the lab part
itens.ok: because I like the lab part

itens.t: I am not sure
alts: yet, but I think I will
yet, but I think I do
already, but I think I will
itens.ok: yet, but I think I will

itens.t: What I like
alts: it is working with people
is work with people
is working with people

itens.t: If it does not work out, I
alts: will did something else
would do something else
would did something else

sec5.pt: Cada frase começa de um jeito. Escolha o final que combina. São as cinco formas que você pode usar na sua aula — o fato, o motivo, a dúvida, o que você gosta, e o plano B.

abertura: Nina is sixteen, she arrived last week, and she has never been to Brazil.

callout.texto:
Not about school. About her: where she was before, what she misses, what she thought Brazil would be like.

One of the three has to be a question you would actually be curious about — in your lesson you can ask it, and she will answer.

sec6.pt:
A Nina tem dezesseis anos, chegou semana passada e nunca veio ao Brasil. Escreva três perguntas para ela.

Não sobre escola. Sobre ela: onde morava antes, do que sente falta, o que imaginava que o Brasil fosse. Uma das três tem de ser uma pergunta que você teria curiosidade de fazer de verdade — na sua aula você pode fazê-la, e vai ouvir a resposta.

itens.t: I am in my last year.
itens.porque: Where he is. Four words, and everything else in his answer hangs off it.

itens.t: I do biology and chemistry.
itens.porque: The second fact, and the only piece of information Nina could not have guessed.

itens.t: Because I want to study medicine.
itens.porque: It explains the two subjects. Without it, the subjects are just a list.

itens.t: Honestly I am not sure yet.
itens.porque: Said out loud, in the middle of the answer, and the conversation does not stop. This is the sentence most people never say in a second language.

itens.t: What I like is the part where you actually help someone.
itens.porque: The real reason, and it is not the same as the first one. Notice it survives even if medicine does not.

itens.t: If medicine does not work out I would still want something with people in it.
itens.porque: Doubt with a plan inside it. It is the answer to a question Nina has not asked yet — and she is about to.

gd22.rationale: Two facts, two reasons, two doubts. Take the doubts out and it sounds rehearsed; take the reasons out and there is nothing to ask about.

itens.t: Let me think. I suppose I would do something else with people in it.
itens.porque: Buys three seconds and then answers. The phrase at the front is from the lesson before this one, and it works here without a change.

itens.t: Honestly? I have never thought about it.
itens.porque: True, short, and it keeps you talking. Saying you have not thought about something is an answer — refusing to answer is not.

itens.t: I do not know.
itens.porque: The same idea with the door closed. Three words and there is nothing for the other person to do with them.

itens.t: I am not sure yet, but I know I want something with people in it.
itens.porque: Doubt and direction in one sentence. This is the strongest answer on the list, and it is the shape from the model.

itens.t: It will work out.
itens.porque: It answers a question nobody asked and avoids the one that was. The conversation now has nowhere to go.

itens.t: Sorry, my English is not good enough for that question.
itens.porque: It is almost never true, and it is always the end of the conversation. The three phrases above cost the same effort and keep you in it.

un22.rationale: The three that work all do the same two things: they buy a little time and they say something. The three that do not work all close the door, politely.

abertura: Three kinds of sentence, and you need all three.

tabela: I am in my last year. I do biology and chemistry.
Because I want to… · What I like is…
I am not sure yet, but… · If it does not work out, I would…

callout.texto:
You read two people disagreeing and said what you thought, with reasons. You kept a conversation going with someone who disagreed with you. You asked six questions and found out three things. And today you talked about yourself for two minutes, twice — once with nothing, and once with an hour behind you.

The difference between those two is the whole point of these four lessons.

abertura: Record the two minutes one more time, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
The same conversation, alone, with nobody asking you anything.

What you are trying to do: two minutes without stopping — the fact, the reason, the doubt, and one question you would ask back.

abertura: Keep it if you record it. In sixteen lessons you will want to hear it again.
speakmore.pt:
Grave os dois minutos mais uma vez, se quiser. É opcional: nada aqui é corrigido nem cobrado na próxima aula.

A mesma conversa, sozinha, sem ninguém perguntando nada: o fato, o motivo, a dúvida, e uma pergunta que você faria de volta.

Se gravar, guarde. Daqui a dezesseis aulas você vai querer ouvir isso de novo.

abertura: Write the message you would send Nina that evening, after the break.

callout.titulo: Six lines, and one of them is a question
callout.texto:
Say one thing you forgot to tell her, one thing you thought about after the conversation, and ask her the question you did not get to ask.

Write it the way you would actually message someone — short lines, and no perfect sentences required.

writemore.pt:
Escreva a mensagem que você mandaria para a Nina naquela noite, depois do intervalo.

Seis linhas: uma coisa que você esqueceu de contar, uma coisa em que pensou depois da conversa, e a pergunta que você não teve tempo de fazer. Escreva como você mandaria mensagem de verdade — linhas curtas, sem precisar de frase perfeita.
